review.checked:
I checked Lemma 20's statement and proof line by line against the definitions of A_sigma and Lambda_sigma in Section 8.2, the line sign s_ell (Section 2, line 186: P_u P_v P_{u+v} = s_ell I, independent of order) and the notation paragraph of Section 8.7.

Proof steps checked:
- Distinct Hermitian Paulis P_v = i^{a.c} X^a Z^c are Hilbert-Schmidt orthogonal, so they form a basis of V and dim V = |O|.
- If s in H anticommutes with p in O, its term in the anticommutator vanishes.
- If s commutes with p, then s != p (H and O are disjoint), so q = s+p lies in X by the closure property. Also q lies in O, because <q,d> = <s,d> + <p,d> = 0 + 1 = 1.
- From P_s P_p P_q = s_L I and P_q^2 = I we get P_s P_p = P_p P_s = s_L P_q, with the sign exactly as in Lambda.
- Given p, the map s -> s+p is injective and q determines s = p+q, so no entry is counted twice. Every q in O that commutes with p is reached, since p+q lies in X (closure) and in d^perp. This is the content of "exactly one point in H on every line through p".
- No coefficient of P_p itself can appear (that would need s = 0), which matches the zero diagonal. Lambda is symmetric.
- Psi(P_p) = sum_q Lambda_{qp} P_q, which is the column convention for the matrix of a map, so Lambda has the spectrum of Psi restricted to V.

Closure property, checked by hand:
- For q_0(a|c) = a.c, q_0(u+v) = q_0(u) + q_0(v) + B(u,v), so on commuting u, v the form q_c = q_0 + B(c,.) is additive and Q_c is closed. u+v != 0 because u != v.
- e^perp is a subspace, so intersecting with it keeps closure.
- A cone with vertex e over a closed base Y in e^perp is closed: two lifts of the same base point sum to e, the vertex, which is in X; lifts of distinct commuting base points y, y' sum to a lift of y+y'.
- All nine configurations of [J3, Table 1] fit these four types: C1 = W; C3 = Q+; C5 = Q_c with c = Y on qubit 0; C6, C11, C14 = cones, which are also W, Q+, Q- cut by e^perp; C8 = PAR = Q+ cut by e^perp; C12 = CP; C15 = CM. This agrees with [J3]'s own line-closedness remark.

Section 8.6 step (v) pointer: it is accurate and not circular. Lemma 20 does not depend on Section 8.6. Since A = C (+) D and P_p = [[0, M_p], [M_p^T, 0]], the top-right block of Psi(P_p) is (1/2)(C M_p + M_p D). So Lemma 20 transports to the M_p basis, and the k^2 matrices M_p are an orthogonal basis of the real k x k matrices.

Configurations: W, Q+, Q_c (c = Y on qubit 0), HW = W cut by Z^perp, CP, CM, and PAR (Q+ cut by Y^perp). For each, d was a random point and sigma a random sign carrier.
- Every configuration passed the closure check.

Hand algebra:
- With P_d = Z (x) I, the top-right block of X(x)P' is P' and of Y(x)P' is -iP'. So M goes from P_d = -1 to P_d = +1, and the -i is right.
- For T = [[0,M],[M^dag,0]] and A = C (+) D, the top-right block of (AT+TA)/2 is (CM+MD)/2.
- theta_c^{-1} = conj(P_c) conj(.), so Theta_c(T) = P_c conj(T) P_c. Also conj(P_v) = (-1)^{q_0(v)} P_v, which gives Theta_c(P_v) = (-1)^{q_c(v)} P_v.
- X(x)P' and Y(x)P' have q_c values that differ by 1, because c (Y on qubit 0) does not touch qubit N-1. So |O| = k^2.
- P_c = I_2 (x) J. J = I for c = 0, and J = Y on qubit 0 of the block for C5, which really is inside the block for N >= 2. J conj(J) = +I and -I respectively.
- The top-right block of P_c conj(T) P_c is J conj(M) J. The map M -> J conj(M) J is an involution for either sign, because conj(J) J = conj(J conj(J)) = +-I. Its fixed set U has U (+) iU = everything and real dimension k^2.
- In C5 the section and R are as stated: q_c(I(x)P''(x)s) = q_0(P'') + [s != I]. Also d lies in Q_c, and Q_c is elliptic.
- The C1 sign identity eps(P_{a,c}) P_{a,c} = (-1)^{c.u_a} i X^a Z^c holds, (E10) holds by the coset character sum, and C = -I + 2k|t><t| + k sum(E_a + iJ_a).
- With tr C = k and tr D = -k, (E8) gives (kappa k/8) tr A^3 - (3/2) kappa k^2 |R| + 3 kappa k^2 r_D. So the difference is -3 kappa k^2 r with r = r_D(tau).
